description.narrative: I korthet syftar projektet att främja inkluderande, klimatsmart ekonomisk utveckling i mejerisektorn med fokus på aktörer med bristande resurser och möjligheter, särskilt kvinnor och ungdomar, längs med värdekedjan för mejeriprodukter

In brief, the aim of the project is to to enable inclusive, climate-smart economic development in the dairy sector, with an emphasis on resource-poor, opportunity-constrained stakeholders, particularly women and youth, across the dairy value chain.

The DNA-BILD's overall objective is to contribute to transform Tanzania's dairy industry by creating vibrant ecosystems of farmer-allied and environmentally sustainable enterprises that improve nutrition, enhance livelihoods, and stimulate inclusive economic growth. The theory of change sets farmer-allied enterprises (FAEs), thus small-medium enterprises with strong links to farmers, to achieve long-term growth and to sustainably scale the benefits both upstream to farmers and farmer livelihoods, and downstream to improve nutrition of consumers. The enterprises are positioned to strategically and intentionally supply and/or source from smallholder farmers in a way that strengthens their capacity, improves their productivity, and enhances their livelihoods, resiliency, and adaptation to climate change. This, in turn, will enable the production of affordable, locally produced dairy products improving the consumption of high quality nutritious and safely processed dairy. Furthermore, the project DNA-BILD will build on the learnings, expertise and working methods of the Dairy Nourishes Africa (DNA) consortium and expands the initiatives outreach to underserved populations, particularly women and youth, and enhances programming for climate mitigation and resilience.

title.narrative: Amendment to the grant agreeemnt on diary nourishes Africa building inclusive livelihoods(DNA-BILD) between the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency , Sida and Land O'lakes Venture 37

description.narrative:
The project has four Objective pillars viz: Grow consumer demand, Drive enterprises to their full potential, increase farmer productivity and strengthen the operating environment. Below some examples of the results achieved in each pillar.
PILLAR 1: Grow consumer demand: The target for the whole project life was to reach 10,000 dairy consumers through various tailored activities and outcomes including consumption Campaigns for dairy products and technical advice and business development of Farmer Allied Enterprises (FAE) for last mile delivery. This target was reached during the second year of implementation. By combining a wide spectrum on activities, the report show that this pillar is achieved by more than double the target. The Embassy has assessed that this can seem to be easily reached either by combining and counting various activities or the target was too low or both. During the 2024 amendment a dialogue resolved to include the dissemination/insemination of sexed semen from Viking Genetics in this pillar which is also related to increasing productivity. The results for this are expected to be reported in 2025 report
PILLAR 2: Drive enterprises to their full potential: DNA BILD uses a capacity scorecard, which explores progress in different operational areas of medium and small-scale Farmer-Allied Enterprises (FAEs). The 2024 Annual Capacity Scorecard has reported significant improvement compared to 2023 because of the capacity building that partner deployed during the reporting period to address weaknesses observed in 2023. The capacity building targeted the areas of dairy products development and/or improvements such as cheese, yoghurt, etc.
The key integral part of targeted interventions for increased innovative commercialization of FAEs. The project provides small by competitive innovative challenge funds. It is matching grants with a maximum of USD 5 000 worth of capital expenditure investment. During the reporting period 32 FAEs benefited from these challenge funds. Total value of challenge fund grants worth USD 85,552 was spent from the contribution with FAEs matching value of USD 72 000 own investments, which is equivalent to 46%. The challenge funds investments are mainly in improving milk processing capacity, efficiency as well as the quality of dairy products. The funds therefore are used in FAEs milk handling equipment such as milk collection and transportation cans, storage and naturalization tanks, processing equipment for various dairy products, packaging etc.
As a results of these investments, the FAEs has reported a 73% increase in the value of sales. The report also highlights an outstanding case of women owned diary processing FAE whose sales increased by 178% in a year as a result of this co-investment challenge funds in diary processing as well as opening new distribution outlets.
PILLAR 3: Increase farmer productivity:
From the project document, the interventions to realize this objective pillar includes promotion dairy genetic gain through artificial insemination using sexed semen, improved animal nutrition though fodder establishment, silage and hay making (for dry season feeding), improved management including housing, hygiene and milk handling. During the year the project continued to coach farmers on the management of established fodder plot including growing of multipurpose trees through distribution of different varieties of seedlings including Sesbania, Calliandra, and Gliricidia species.
A total of 12,280 seedlings were distributed to 750 smallholder dairy farmers in the project area. A total of 400 smallholder dairy farmers in Tanga regions received 4000 MPTs while 350 smallholder dairy farmers in Arusha and Kilimanjaro received 8,280 MPTS. Cumulatively, DNA-BILD has promoted the planting of 42,400 multipurpose trees through 2,917 smallholder dairy farmers in the project area. Farmers are also trained and adopted feeds conservation through silage and hay making.
With DNA-BILD facilitation 3,200 doses of sexed semen from Viking Genetics in Denmark are imported and granted to the Government of Tanzania through the National Artificial Insemination Centre (NAIC) in Usa River, Arusha region. The project continued with promotion and distribution of sexed semen and 212 doses are reported to be administered from March to December 2024. The use of sexed semen produces, on average, a 93% likelihood of female calves being born.
The income indicator: Venture 37 measure the annual farmer income from value of annual sales in both formal and informal markets. The report uses the data from the projects household survey which reports an average increase of 58% of annual income for a smallholder dairy farmer supported by DNA-BILD. The increase in annual farmer income is attributed to above objective pillars: the increased milk productivity by farmers cows, processing high quality dairy products and consumption promotion.
Pillar 4: Strengthen the Operating Environment: The Embassy assess that the cooperation partner did not do much on this pillar, save the participation in stakeholders meetings. The main issue reported to be discussed for advocacy to the government authorities is the shortage livestock and dairy extension personnel. The report does not show any specific policy issues that was raised by the project. Furthermore, although the attribution to this project did not clarify, the report indicates that the Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries (MLF) recruited 300 new extension officers to begin to bridge the gap and distributed to various districts in Tanzania, bringing the total number of extension officers in Tanzania to 3,800.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
